title: Children differ in inborn style from the start
summary: OpenStax says children bring an inborn style: some show positive feelings and adjust readily, and some show negative feelings and adjust less readily.
body: OpenStax Psychology describes innate traits that influence how a person thinks, behaves, and reacts. Children it calls easy show positive feelings, modify well to change, and can regulate their feelings. Children it calls difficult show negative feelings and have difficulty adjusting and regulating those feelings. The page says difficult children are much more likely to challenge caregivers, citing Thomas, 1984, which was not opened here. It also says it is possible that easy children draw warmer care and that irritable children evoke irritation. That possibility is the textbook's suggestion, not a rule that a child's style causes a caregiver's response. The textbook's own name for these traits is recorded in the source note.

sources.title: 9.3 Stages of Development
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: Supports the temperament definition and the easy-versus-difficult contrast. OpenStax Psychology, first edition (publish date 2014-12-08), CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase of the opened page; the cited primary paper was not opened. The page's word for these innate traits is temperament.
